mainTopic: How responsible is a finder for lost money he holds, and can רב יוסף, who says a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר, explain the dispute between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא?
overview: The amud opens with the end of a statement limiting the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא: they argue only when the finder used the money. If he did not use it and it was lost, everyone agrees he is exempt. The גמרא asks whether this refutes רב יוסף, who holds that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר and pays for theft and loss. רב יוסף answers that everyone agrees the finder pays for theft and loss, and the argument is only about אונסין, which only a שואל pays for. The גמרא challenges him from the word לפיכך in רבי עקיבא's statement. That word teaches something if the argument is about theft and loss, but seems extra on רב יוסף's reading. The answer is that רבי עקיבא said לפיכך only to match רבי טרפון's wording. רבי טרפון's own לפיכך teaches a real point: since the רבנן permitted him to use the money, it is as if he used it. The amud ends with a new challenge to רב יוסף: the משנה says 'if they were lost,' which sounds like loss, not אונסין. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute applies only when the finder used the money
steps.stepSummary: The end of a statement that limits the argument: if the finder did not use the money and it was lost, everyone agrees he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only when he used the money. But if he did not use it and it got lost, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of a statement that narrows the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא to a case where the finder used the money. If he never used it, everyone agrees he does not pay if it is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement draws a clear line. Using the money is what could make the finder liable. Without use, he pays nothing for a loss according to everyone. This 'everyone agrees he is exempt' becomes the basis for the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: only when he used them.
But if he did not use them,
if they were lost, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a statement begun before this section, limiting the scope of the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only when the finder used the money. If he did not use it, everyone agrees he is exempt for loss.

steps.title: Does this refute רב יוסף?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ruling just stated contradicts רב יוסף, who holds that one guarding a lost item is like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this refutes רב יוסף? It was stated: about one guarding a lost item, רבה says he is like an unpaid guard, and רב יוסף says he is like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against רב יוסף. It quotes his argument with רבה about how responsible a finder is for the lost item he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר pays for theft and loss, while a שומר חנם pays only for negligence. Step 1 said everyone agrees the finder is exempt if the money was lost. That sounds like he is only a שומר חנם, as רבה holds, and against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: someone guarding a lost item he found
an unpaid guard; pays only if he was negligent
a paid guard; also pays for theft and loss

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב יוסף?
For it was stated: one who guards a lost item,
רבה said: he is like an unpaid guard;
רב יוסף said: he is like a paid guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling in step 1 to attack רב יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שומר שכר pays for loss. Yet step 1 says everyone exempts the finder who did not use the money and it was lost.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the argument is about borrower-level accidents
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says everyone agrees the finder pays for theft and loss. The dispute is whether he also pays for אונסין, like a borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף can say: for theft and loss everyone agrees he is liable. They argue about accidents that only a borrower pays for. רבי טרפון holds the rabbis let him use the money, so he is a borrower of it. רבי עקיבא holds they did not let him use it, so he is not a borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself by moving the dispute to a different kind of damage. On his reading, 'lost' in the statement means lost through an אונס, an event beyond his control.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone treats the finder as at least a שומר שכר, so he pays for theft and loss. The only question is whether he is a שואל, who also pays for אונסין. That depends on whether he was permitted to use the money. When he did not use it, the exemption refers only to אונסין, so רב יוסף is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: a borrower; pays even for accidents

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the levels: a שומר שכר pays for theft and loss, but only a שואל pays for אונסין. רב יוסף places the whole dispute at the שואל level.

phrases.english: רב יוסף can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: בִּגְנֵיבָה וַאֲבֵידָה – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחַיָּיב,
phrases.english: In theft and loss, everyone agrees that he is liable;
where they argue is about accidents, which a borrower pays for.
רבי טרפון holds:
the rabbis permitted him to use them,
so he is a borrower of them.
And רבי עקיבא holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שָׁרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְאִשְׁתַּמּוֹשֵׁי בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: the rabbis did not permit him to use them,
therefore he is not a borrower of them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the subject of the dispute: from theft and loss to אונסין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute and the exemption are about theft and loss, which would contradict רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone holds the finder liable for theft and loss. The exemption and the dispute concern only אונסין, which depend on whether he counts as a שואל.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא say 'therefore'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's reading: the word לפיכך in רבי עקיבא's statement fits only if the dispute is about theft and loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does רבי עקיבא say 'therefore'? It makes sense if they argue about theft and loss. That is why the משנה says: 'רבי עקיבא says he may not use them; therefore, if they are lost, he is not responsible for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's answer from the wording of the משנה, focusing on the word 'לפיכך' in רבי עקיבא's statement. Here it starts showing that the word fits a dispute about theft and loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא links two ideas: since he may not use the money, he is exempt if it is lost. The challenge here is about the word 'therefore' itself: it must teach something, and it teaches something only if the dispute is about theft and loss. Step 5 explains what it would teach on that reading, and step 6 shows it would teach nothing on רב יוסף's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense if you say...

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need the 'therefore' that רבי עקיבא said?
It makes sense if you say
that they argue about theft and loss;
that is why it teaches:
'רבי עקיבא says: he may not use them,'

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם אָבְדוּ – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן״.
phrases.english: 'therefore, if they are lost, he is not responsible for them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לְפִיכָךְ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 3 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim in step 3 that the dispute is only about אונסין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's 'therefore, if lost, exempt' links not using the money to an exemption for loss. That link fits a dispute about theft and loss, not about אונסין.

steps.title: Explaining why 'therefore' fits a theft-and-loss dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge. Without לפיכך we might think the finder is a שומר שכר, as רב יוסף holds. 'Therefore' teaches that since he may not use the money, he is not a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought he is a paid guard, as רב יוסף says, and liable for theft and loss. So 'therefore' teaches us: now that he may not use the money, he is not a paid guard and is not liable for theft and loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the word 'לפיכך' fits only a dispute about theft and loss. This completes the challenge against רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, being allowed to use the money is what would make the finder a שומר שכר. 'Therefore' tells us that רבי עקיבא, who forbids use, removes that status and with it liability for theft and loss. On this reading, רבי עקיבא's own words say a non-using finder is not a שומר שכר, which goes against רב יוסף.
steps.whatToRemember: This is the first half of a two-part challenge. On a theft-and-loss reading, 'לפיכך' teaches that a finder who may not use the money is not a שומר שכר. Step 6 shows that on רב יוסף's reading the word adds nothing, and step 7 answers the challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא using one small connecting word in the משנה to decide what level of responsibility is being argued about.

phrases.english: You might have thought
that he is a paid guard, as רב יוסף holds,
and is liable for theft and loss;
so 'therefore' teaches us otherwise.
Now that you said he may not use them,
he is not a paid guard
and is not liable for theft and loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר הָוֵי כִּדְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 4 by explaining what 'לפיכך' adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר, and his answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Therefore' teaches that a finder forbidden to use the money is not a שומר שכר and is exempt for theft and loss. That directly opposes רב יוסף.

steps.title: Under רב יוסף, רבי עקיבא's 'therefore' looks unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If everyone agrees the finder pays for theft and loss, and the argument is only about אונסין like a שואל, then רבי עקיבא's לפיכך adds nothing. The משנה could simply have said 'he may not use it,' and we would already know he is not a שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that for theft and loss everyone agrees he must pay, and they only argue about accidents, which a borrower pays for, then what does רבי עקיבא's 'therefore' mean? The משנה should have said only: 'רבי עקיבא says he may not use the money.' I would already know that since he may not use it, he is not a borrower and does not have to pay. So why do I need רבי עקיבא's 'therefore'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge to רב יוסף. It shows that under his reading, רבי עקיבא's word 'therefore' is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the גמרא showed that לפיכך makes sense if the argument is about theft and loss. Now it shows the other side: if the argument is only about אונסין, the word teaches nothing new. Once you know he may not use the money, it is obvious he is not a שואל, so he does not pay for אונסין.

keyTerms.meaning: But if you say (introduces the other way of reading)
A borrower, who pays even for accidents

phrases.english: But if you say
that in theft and loss everyone
does not disagree that he is liable,
and where they disagree is about accidents, which a borrower pays for,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's reading from step 3.

phrases.english: what is the 'therefore' of Rabbi Akiva?
This is how it should have taught:
'Rabbi Akiva says: He may not use them,'
and I would know that since
he may not use them,
he is not a borrower
and is not responsible to pay for them.
So why do I need Rabbi Akiva's 'therefore'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּגְנֵיבָה וַאֲבֵידָה דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge begun in steps 4-5 by showing the problem under רב יוסף's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the argument is about אונסין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב יוסף, the word לפיכך in רבי עקיבא's statement would be unnecessary, because 'he may not use it' already shows he is not a שואל

steps.title: רבי עקיבא said 'therefore' to match רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא's לפיכך really is extra. He said it only to mirror the לפיכך in רבי טרפון's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said because of רבי טרפון's 'therefore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. It admits the word is extra and explains that it is there only to match the other opinion's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון said 'he may use it; therefore if lost he pays.' To keep the two opinions parallel, רבי עקיבא's opinion was worded the same way: 'he may not use it; therefore he does not pay.' So the extra word is about style, not a new law.

phrases.english: Because of Rabbi Tarfon's 'therefore.'
phrases.notes: He means: רבי עקיבא's wording copies רבי טרפון's, so the two opinions sound alike.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic parallelism: the extra word is explained as matching the other opinion's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's לפיכך must teach something new, which only fits the theft-and-loss reading
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is there only to mirror רבי טרפון, so רב יוסף's reading still stands

steps.title: Why does רבי טרפון need 'therefore'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי טרפון's own לפיכך adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need רבי טרפון's 'therefore'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי טרפון's statement and asks what his 'therefore' teaches. This sets up the next step's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא's לפיכך only copies רבי טרפון's, then רבי טרפון's own word must have a real reason. The גמרא asks what that reason is.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks what a word adds)

phrases.english: And why do I need Rabbi Tarfon's 'therefore'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 7: if רבי עקיבא's word copies רבי טרפון's, what does רבי טרפון's word teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law רבי טרפון's לפיכך teaches

steps.title: Permission to use counts as if he used it
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון's לפיכך teaches that since the רבנן allowed the finder to use the money, he is treated as if he already used it. So he is responsible like a borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: since the רבנן allowed him to use the money, it is as if he used it, and he is responsible for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי טרפון's 'therefore' teaches a real new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person becomes a שואל only by actually using the item. רבי טרפון's לפיכך teaches that being allowed to use it is enough. Even if he never touched the money, he pays like a שואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי טרפון's word carries real meaning, which explains why רבי עקיבא's matching word can be just for style.

phrases.english: This is what he means:
Since the Sages permitted him
to use them,
it is as if he used them,
and he is responsible for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְאִשְׁתַּמּוֹשֵׁי בְּגַוַּיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי טרפון's לפיכך teaches that permission to use the money makes him responsible as if he had used it

steps.title: But the משנה says 'were lost'
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to רב יוסף: the משנה speaks of the money being lost (אבדו). That is loss, not אונסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'if they were lost'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem for רב יוסף. The משנה's own word points to loss, not accidents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said everyone agrees the finder pays for loss, and they argue only about אונסין. But the משנה says 'if they were lost, he pays / does not pay.' So the argument seems to be about loss itself, against רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (introduces a challenge from a source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different challenge from the לפיכך challenge. Before, the problem was the word 'therefore'; now the problem is the word 'lost.'

phrases.english: But it teaches 'were lost'!
phrases.notes: The משנה says 'therefore, if they were lost.' Loss is exactly what רב יוסף said nobody argues about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב יוסף on the word לפיכך, the גמרא attacks him from a different word in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the argument is only about אונסין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says 'אבדו' (lost), which shows the argument is about loss, the case רב יוסף said everyone agrees on
